arabic_locator.text: قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرِ بْنُ جَرِيرٍ: وَالصَّوَابُ قَوْلُ مَنْ قَالَ: مَعْنَى ذَلِكَ: فَاجْعَلْ صَلَاتَكَ كُلَّهَا لِرَبِّكَ خَالِصًا دُونَ مَا سِوَاهُ مِنَ الْأَنْدَادِ وَالْآلِهَةِ  وَكَذَلِكَ نَحْرَكَ اجْعَلْهُ لَهُ دُونَ الْأَوْثَانِ؛ شُكْرًا لَهُ عَلَى مَا أَعْطَاكَ مِنَ الْكَرَامَةِ وَالْخَيْرِ، الَّذِي لَا كِفَاء لَهُ، وَخَصَّكَ بِهِ.

roles.Abu_Jafar_ibn_Jarir: named quoted exegete, distinct from Abu Jafar al-Baqir in A02

semantic_units.statement_en: Ibn Jarir identifies as correct the interpretation that all prayer is to be devoted exclusively to the Lord, excluding other rivals and deities.
Ibn Jarir likewise interprets the sacrifice as being devoted to the Lord rather than idols.
The quoted interpretation presents this as gratitude for the honor and good uniquely bestowed on the addressee, described as without equivalent.

fidelity_notes: Maintain Ibn Jarir as quoted voice; do not replace him with Ibn Kathir.
Separate later Ibn Kathir commendation in P02 from Q01 quoted preference.
Do not confuse Ibn Jarir with al-Baqir solely because both use Abu Jafar.
No independent edition or Tabari source locator verified by this Ibn Kathir quotation.
English statements are analytical paraphrases; bounded English absence retained.
remaining: Choose bounded proposition design preserving exclusive devotion and gratitude scope
Validate nested speaker distinction and absence of invented direct-source verification
